title: Predict the output: parent reference calling static method
shortTitle: Predict the output: parent reference calling static method
keyPoints: Static methods are resolved by REFERENCE type (compile time), not object type (runtime)
Parent p = new Child(); p.staticMethod() calls Parent's version, not Child's
This is method hiding, not overriding – no polymorphism for statics
Understanding this concept is essential for Java interviews at senior level
This concept directly affects how banking applications manage resources

s1_definition.oneliner: The parent's static method is called because static methods are resolved by reference type at compile time, not by object type at runtime.
s1_definition.profdef:
Static method hiding:

- `Parent p = new Child();` – reference type is Parent.
- `p.greet()` (static) → resolved by reference type → Parent.greet().
- Instance methods would call Child's version (polymorphism). Static methods do not participate in polymorphism.
s1_definition.analogy: See Q12 (Keywords: static) and Q37 (Can main be overridden) for full explanation.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Parent p = new Child();
  p.greet();  (static)
    → compile time: reference type = Parent
    → calls Parent.greet()
    → output: "Parent"

  If instance method:
    p.greet();  (instance, overridden)
    → runtime: object type = Child
    → calls Child.greet()
    → output: "Child"
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Static methods are resolved by reference type at compile time. Parent p = new Child(); p.staticMethod() calls the Parent's version. This is hiding, not overriding.

One sentence to remember: static = reference type wins (compile time), instance = object type wins (runtime).
